data.content_ref: inline:The proposed evidence ('Cross-Substrate Invariance') is a necessary but insufficient condition for true independence. The target's own countercondition admits a non-substrate shared cause (a logic bug in a common library used across all substrates). Under that countercondition, failures could perfectly satisfy cross-substrate invariance—different substrates are unaffected by the substrate-based partition—yet remain highly correlated due to the shared library bug. Thus 'Cross-Substrate Invariance' cannot distinguish truly independent failures from pseudo-uncorrelated ones in exactly the class of cases the problem asks about.
